overview.description: Eight-card Golf: 2+ players, 52 cards. Each has 8 cards in layout (e.g. 2Ã—4). Draw or take discard to replace; aim for lowest point total. Same scoring as 4/6-card Golf; larger layout. Play 9 or 18 holes.

history.origins: Golf is widespread in North America and Britain; the eight-card form extends six-card Golf with a larger layout (four columns of two cards per player). It is less widespread than 4- and 6-card Golf. The variant was documented on Bill Whitnack's Card Games site, using a double 52-card deck with jokers for larger groups.

setup.players: Two to eight players. A standard 52-card pack is used; with more than four players, a second pack (and optionally jokers) may be used.
setup.dealing: 8 cards each in layout; stock and discard.

rules.objective: Lowest point total in 8-card layout. Replace cards by draw or discard; hand ends per house rules (e.g. when one player has all face up or after knock).
rules.gameplay: As 4/6-card Golf: draw or take discard, replace one layout card. Standard Golf scoring.

variations.name: Eight Card Golf with Jokers
variations.description: Double 52-card deck with four jokers; pair in column scores zero; two equal pairs in any two columns minus 10; jokers minus 5. Nine deals. (Bill Whitnack variant.)

scoring.description: Lowest point total in 8-card layout wins the hole; numeral cards face value, J/Q 10, King 0. Play 9 or 18 holes; lowest cumulative score wins.
scoring.winCondition: Lowest point total in 8-card layout wins; after 9 or 18 deals the player with the lowest cumulative score wins.
